pr_title: Allow using integer vectors for iteration and make range() use them
pr_body:
This fixes #34121. Since it causes failures with large values, and because floats aren't ideal for integer iteration anyway, we don't want to optimize range's parameters into Vector2/Vector3. Instead, let's use Vector2i/Vector3i which have a larger range (and might perform better).

Using Vector2i/Vector3i still has a limit at 2^31, which is lower than what normal GDScript ints allow (2^63), but I tried removing the optimization entirely and it still fails at 2^31 anyway. If it's ever desired to go above 2^31, that can wait for later, and I don't think I'll be the one doing that.

Using Vector2i/Vector3i as iterators also means that we can directly use them instead of the word "range", which may be useful if you want to store a range in a variable.

Here's some test code:

```gdscript
	for i in Vector2(16777213, 16777221):
		print(i) # Fails at the last value because 16777221 becomes 16777220.
		# At least, this will fail as long as real_t is float, but it would work when real_t is double.
	print("====")
	for i in Vector2i(16777213, 16777221):
		print(i) # Works.
	print("====")
	for i in range(16777213, 16777221):
		print(i) # Works.
	print("====")
```

I also changed a function that returns a `bool` value so that its return type is also `bool`, used `int64_t` in a few places where the end result becomes `int64_t` anyway, and I did a little formatting in the beginning of `variant_op.cpp` because it wasn't aligned before and it was ugly.
pr_comments:
What about changing Vector2/3 iteration to use float start/end/increment, instead of casting them to int (thus reverting #8783)?
That would allow for things like `for angle in Vector3(0.0, 2 * PI, PI / 10)`

Does using `Vector2i()` instead of `range()` avoid allocating a GDScript array? If so, this can perform much better when iterating over a large range. We should make sure to document this :slightly_smiling_face:

Likewise, using an integer as an iteration value (`5` instead of `range(5)`) is faster for this reason.
@Calinou `for i in range(x,y)` has been converted to `for i in Vector2(x, y)` ever since bfef8de1bc4f7a7b9617a7b181881129033a0b0e

issue_context.title: range(x,y) malfunctions for values greater than 0x1000000
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
Godot_v3.1.2-stable_win64

**Issue description:**
Using range(x,y) with values greater than 0x1000000 (16777216), where x and/or y are odd, results in an incorrect array with one or two extra values (as if x were x-1 and/or y were y+1).

Here is a code snippet to show this:
```
   for i in range(16777213, 16777215):
      print(i)
   print("====")
   for i in range(16777217, 16777219):
      print(i)
   print("====")
```

Its output is:
```
16777213
16777214
====
16777216
16777217
16777218
16777219
====
```

The former is correct, the latter is wrong.

P.S. The bug is slightly more complex than I had described. Not only may it result in one or two extra values; it may also result in one or two missing values. For example, range(16777219, 16777221) returns an empty array.

P.P.S. This bug also affects the range(x,y,step) flavour.
comments:
They might have been converted to `float`, `16777216` is the maximum integer value they can accurately represent (I wonder if anyone knowingly uses it as floats? tbh I see no reason why they would be)

Note: careful not to start from 0, a range of 16777216 means the array it returns allocates about 536 megabytes, that's quite epic to just iterate with a for loop :p (as per https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/3765#event-570118995)
Updated OP with P.S. and P.P.S.
Another point for integer vectors to be added to the engine... unless there is a way to use some other data structure? `Vector2` and `Vector3` sounds quite an overuse here.
@Zylann I can see `Vector2i` in the codebase, but no `Vector3i`. (`Vector2i` isn't exposed to GDScript though.)

review_comments: Why is this change here? I get that `bool` makes more sense, but it's not related to the other changes.
Because it's a minor fix that I noticed while making this PR and it's easier than making a separate PR just for this one change, but I could do that if you want.
At least do it in a different commit, so the blame is more precise.
